PullRequest.Title: Parent the ConPTY console window to the VS Code window
PullRequest.Body:
- Send the HWND of the window hosting each local terminal to node-pty, which makes it the owner of the terminal's console window. Dialogs that console apps parent to their console window or its owner, like the `Connect-AzAccount` sign-in picker, then open in front of VS Code instead of behind it. Modal ones disable VS Code while they're open, as in Windows Terminal.
- Start the handle lookup when the terminal is created, and send the handle before `start()` for new, revived, and reattached processes, using the window the terminal is in by then. Send it again when `attachToElement()` moves the terminal to another window.
- Read the handle with `IHostService.getNativeWindowHandle` and send its bytes to the pty host unchanged as a `VSBuffer`, since node-pty takes the `Buffer` that Electron's `getNativeWindowHandle()` returns. Skip remote terminals, and never fail terminal startup if the lookup, the IPC, or the node-pty call fails.
- Add `setParentWindow` along the `clearBuffer` IPC path. The pty host calls node-pty's `setParentWindow` right after `spawn()`, before node-pty launches the shell, or right away if the pty is already running, and trace-logs whether it was sent. Only on Windows with `windowsUseConptyDll`.
- Keep the handle out of `ITerminalProcessOptions`, which are persisted for revive and would replay a stale HWND.
- Add `terminal.integrated.windowsReparentConsoleWindow` (default on, ExP-controllable) to turn this off without turning off conpty.dll.
- Add `TerminalProcessManager` tests for sending the handle before `start()`, window moves, startup races, passing the handle bytes through unchanged, and the setting.
- If a dialog's process dies while the dialog is modal to VS Code, VS Code stays disabled. That's tracked in microsoft/node-pty#996.
- Bump `node-pty` to `1.2.0-beta.17`, which adds `setParentWindow` from microsoft/node-pty#995.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The IPC path mirrors `clearBuffer`: [`LocalPty.clearBuffer`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3b0232e709b18b1adc4260c9273aef32b43c0f36/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/electron-browser/localPty.ts#L64-L66), [`IPtyService.clearBuffer`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3b0232e709b18b1adc4260c9273aef32b43c0f36/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/terminal.ts#L357), [`PtyService.clearBuffer`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3b0232e709b18b1adc4260c9273aef32b43c0f36/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L391-L394), [`PersistentTerminalProcess.clearBuffer`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3b0232e709b18b1adc4260c9273aef32b43c0f36/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L921-L924), and [`TerminalProcess.clearBuffer`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3b0232e709b18b1adc4260c9273aef32b43c0f36/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/terminalProcess.ts#L579-L581).
- Storing the handle until spawn and reparenting live once running comes from Windows Terminal's [`ConptyConnection::ReparentWindow`](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/9e6cf223ddb7d62eba85254ed88f8e2d663a172e/src/cascadia/TerminalConnection/ConptyConnection.cpp#L645-L659); reparenting before the client launches comes from [`ConptyConnection::Start`](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/9e6cf223ddb7d62eba85254ed88f8e2d663a172e/src/cascadia/TerminalConnection/ConptyConnection.cpp#L409-L426).
- Getting the HWND with `IHostService.getNativeWindowHandle(windowId)` comes from [`MainThreadWindow.registerNativeHandle`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3b0232e709b18b1adc4260c9273aef32b43c0f36/src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadWindow.ts#L40-L49), relying on the per-window memoization in [`NativeHostService.getNativeWindowHandle`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3b0232e709b18b1adc4260c9273aef32b43c0f36/src/vs/workbench/services/host/electron-browser/nativeHostService.ts#L237-L243) instead of a second cache.
- Sending the handle as a `VSBuffer` relies on the IPC protocol [serializing](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3b0232e709b18b1adc4260c9273aef32b43c0f36/src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.ts#L281-L284) and [deserializing](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3b0232e709b18b1adc4260c9273aef32b43c0f36/src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.ts#L311) it as is.
- Keeping the handle out of the launch options comes from [`PtyService.serializeTerminalState`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3b0232e709b18b1adc4260c9273aef32b43c0f36/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L229-L253), which persists `processLaunchConfig` for revive.
- The ExP-controllable setting shape comes from [`terminal.integrated.enableWin32InputMode`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3b0232e709b18b1adc4260c9273aef32b43c0f36/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/terminalConfiguration.ts#L612-L621).


Resolves https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/10198

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call chain is explicit: TerminalInstance invokes this method before createProcess; createProcess awaits _resolveParentWindowHandle; NativeHostService crosses to Electron main on the first lookup per window and memoizes it; LocalPty forwards setParentWindow to the pty host; TerminalProcess drops it when useConptyDll is false. The exact latency varies with IPC load, so severity is low, but the no-op boundary work and trigger are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Electron main-process handle requests, renderer-to-pty-host IPC calls, and serialized handle bytes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The native-handle request is coalesced to one per unique VS Code window by NativeHostService, while the no-op pty-host RPC scales once per terminal startup/restore and once per actual window move.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive IPC and marginally increased terminal startup/restoration latency
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, terminals with windowsUseConptyDll disabled performed neither the native-window-handle lookup nor the setParentWindow pty-host RPC.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Windows local terminals now resolve a native window handle and attempt a setParentWindow call whenever windowsReparentConsoleWindow is enabled, including configurations where windowsUseConptyDll is false and the pty layer cannot use the result.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 782 adds the eligibility guard for the new setParentWindow path but checks only platform, remote authority, and windowsReparentConsoleWindow; it does not check windowsUseConptyDll, even though the newly added TerminalProcess.setParentWindow returns immediately when useConptyDll is false.
Findings.Title: Gate window-handle IPC on conpty.dll
Findings.Impact: On Windows installations that disable terminal.integrated.windowsUseConptyDll, the first terminal in each window is unnecessarily held behind a main-process IPC, and terminal creation/restoration still sends one useless pty-host RPC per terminal. Restoring many terminals adds avoidable IPC traffic and launch work without enabling reparenting.
Findings.Evidence: TerminalInstance calls TerminalProcessManager.setParentWindow before every local terminal creation. The manager's added guard at line 782 allows the call when windowsReparentConsoleWindow=true even if windowsUseConptyDll=false, then createProcess awaits the handle resolution. NativeHostService.getNativeWindowHandle performs one Electron-main request per window, and LocalPty.setParentWindow performs a renderer-to-pty-host RPC per process. The added TerminalProcess.setParentWindow checks !useConptyDll and returns without using the handle, proving all of this work is wasted for that supported configuration.
Findings.Recommendation: Include windowsUseConptyDll in the early eligibility guard (and avoid retaining/resolving a parent handle when it is false), so configurations that cannot call node-pty's reparenting API stay on the previous startup path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create, revive, or reattach local Windows terminals with conpty.dll reparenting enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For a new, revived, or reattached local Windows terminal, backend process-object creation completes first, then createProcess explicitly awaits the latest native-handle lookup before issuing setParentWindow and start. Thus the cold Electron-main lookup is on shell startup's critical path; the setParentWindow RPC is issued immediately before start to preserve ordering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request the Electron native HWND through IHostService.getNativeWindowHandle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold call per unique VS Code window, coalesced across all terminals in that window; zero additional main-process calls on warm cache hits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Terminal startup did not request the native window handle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The awaited lookup must complete before the shell start message is sent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the VSBuffer handle and send it from the renderer to the pty host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new setParentWindow RPC per terminal creation/revival/reattachment when a handle exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The renderer sent create/start-related terminal IPC but no parent-window RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: It is enqueued immediately before start so node-pty can apply the parent after spawn() returns and before the shell launches.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn node-pty and launch the configured shell.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shell subprocess per terminal, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same shell spawn occurred without a preceding setParentWindow call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the existing terminal launch boundary reached after the new parent-window work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of unique VS Code windows for cold native-handle lookups and number of restored/created terminals for pty-host calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent terminal restores share the per-window native-handle Promise, but each terminal independently emits setParentWindow and start messages to the pty host. There is no added shared limiter; effective pty-host concurrency/cardinality follows the number of terminals restored.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: IHostService caches the Promise and result by VS Code window ID, so concurrent terminal creations in one window coalesce to one cold Electron-main lookup; warm creations reuse the resolved handle. Each TerminalProcessManager retains its own 8-byte handle, but the pty-host setParentWindow call is per terminal and is not cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added awaits, cache implementation, direct proxy call chain, and node-pty invocation are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The handle is only eight bytes and the main-process lookup is coalesced, so exact added latency under normal IPC load is uncertain and likely small; the changed critical-path ordering and per-terminal pty RPC are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression on the supported enabled path: the bounded one-per-window lookup is coalesced, the per-terminal RPC is required by the feature, and it is intentionally ordered before shell launch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start or restore Windows terminals when windowsUseConptyDll is disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first terminal in a window still awaits the cold native-handle IPC before start. Every terminal then issues setParentWindow immediately before start; TerminalProcess discards it because useConptyDll is false.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the HWND for a backend that cannot reparent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold Electron-main IPC per unique window; subsequent lookups are warm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The cold request blocks first-terminal startup even though its result cannot be used.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send an eight-byte handle to TerminalProcess.setParentWindow, which rejects the capability via its useConptyDll guard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One renderer-to-pty-host RPC per terminal startup/restore, plus one per actual window move.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The startup call is issued directly before start and consumes serialization/dispatch work; the pty implementation returns without using it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Unique windows for main-process calls and terminal count/window moves for pty-host calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A multi-terminal restore coalesces the main-process lookup but fans out one useless pty-host RPC per terminal. Those calls are not grouped or suppressed by backend capability.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The same per-window native-handle cache coalesces the Electron-main request, but the resolved handle is still retained by each manager. There is no negative capability cache at the manager layer; every terminal forwards the handle to the pty host despite the backend configuration making it unusable.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the manager omits the prerequisite setting from its guard while the terminal process explicitly no-ops on that setting.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users must explicitly or experimentally disable windowsUseConptyDll, and each individual payload is tiny, so prevalence and milliseconds are uncertain; the wasted boundaries and terminal-count scaling are proven.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity boundary fan-out: the diff adds IPC and startup waiting that cannot produce the requested behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reattach or move a live terminal between VS Code windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: TerminalInstance does not await setParentWindow during attachToElement, so reparenting work is off the synchronous DOM-attachment/render critical path. The pty-host RPC runs asynchronously after the window lookup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the destination window's native handle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold Electron-main request per newly encountered VS Code window globally; cached calls per attached terminal otherwise resolve from the memoized Promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Moving or reattaching terminal DOM did not request an HWND.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the synchronous attachment path because the caller does not await it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply the destination HWND to the live pty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pty-host call per terminal whose effective window handle changed; zero when equality detects the same handle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No live reparenting IPC was sent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and not awaited by DOM attachment, though it consumes pty-host work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of terminal instances moved to a different VS Code window, after deduplication by unchanged handle.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Moving a group of terminals can schedule one independent RPC per terminal. Native-handle lookup is coalesced by destination window, but pty calls are not globally limited.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Moves to an already-seen VS Code window use NativeHostService's cached handle. Reattaching to the same window still performs an async cached lookup, but handle equality suppresses the pty-host RPC; moving to a different window updates the per-manager handle and sends once.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for cardinality and scheduling; low uncertainty only in real-world group sizes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously moved terminals varies, but normal window counts are small and same-window reattachments suppress downstream RPC. No evidence shows a realistic jank or throughput threshold on the supported path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: required live reparenting scales per affected terminal, destination handle reads are coalesced, and the work is not awaited by the UI attachment path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create remote, non-Windows, reparenting-disabled, or custom pseudoterminals
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The guarded non-Windows, remote, and setting-disabled cases add no boundary to startup. A first local custom PTY in a Windows window may wait for the shared cold handle lookup, but this is bounded once per window.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for non-Windows, remote, or explicit reparenting-off cases; at most one cold main-process lookup per window for local Windows custom PTYs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: None of these scenarios requested it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No effect for early-return cases; the custom-PTY cold lookup is awaited before start/open.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Unique VS Code windows rather than custom-PTY count after cache coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Early-return cases perform no added concurrent work. Custom PTYs share the per-window handle Promise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Non-Windows and remote terminals return before lookup. Disabling windowsReparentConsoleWindow also returns before lookup. Local custom PTYs on Windows can populate the same one-per-window handle cache, but their optional setParentWindow method is absent, so no pty RPC follows.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for guards and cache behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Custom PTY prevalence and cold-lookup duration are uncertain; coalescing bounds this to one native request per window, so evidence does not establish a separate material regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: primary guards eliminate work for remote/non-Windows/disabled cases, while custom-PTY overhead is bounded and shares the same cold cache miss.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 14 changed files and every diff page. Traced terminal creation, restore/reattach, live window movement, unsupported backends, native-handle caching, renderer/main/pty-host IPC, and shell spawn ordering. Submitted one low-severity finding for no-op IPC when conpty.dll is disabled; found no unbounded retention, synchronous UI work, concurrency burst, serialization amplification, or evidenced dependency-related regression.
